set.overview: The south slope is the easy way up this 12,520 ft peak above the Owens Valley east of Big Pine. It is a class 2 walk on talus and boulders, reached from a high camp at Red Lake. Expect a long first day of uphill with a pack, then a short summit day. Early in the season the upper bowl holds snow that changes the character of the climb.
set.approach: From there the trail climbs about 3.5 miles and roughly 3,800 feet to Red Lake, staying on the north side of the creek well above the water, and most parties camp at the lake. The climb proper starts at the lake and heads up the bowl to the south of the peak.
hazards: Steep hard snow chute in the upper bowl in early season; crampons and an ice axe are needed to avoid a long slide
Steep loose scree and talus if dropping straight back to the lake
Unavoidable rock field to cross below the chute
Rough road to the trailhead can cut tires

review.notes: Only Tinemaha written. Distances: only a 2-day trip log (trailhead-to-camp 3.5 mi/3,843 ft; summit day 6.85 mi incl. return) so no clean one-way dist or summit gain; skipped gain/dist/descent/season. Skipped Diamond, Baxter (sources describe different lines/trailheads, 'standard route' unclear), Colosseum, Perkins, Harrington, Tehipite, Spanish (only whole-day totals incl. camp), Three Sisters (loop totals), Prater, Bolton Brown, Birch (no per-peak figures; Birch line in reports not clearly the row's).
